WHAT EXISTS · WHERE IT IS · WHO HOLDS IT

Research outputs

Three degrees of research, a consultancy, an internship and a working tool. Some of it is public, some belongs to the organisations it was done for, and the rest is a PDF I will happily send you.

This page says which is which — because a portfolio that lists outputs without saying whether anyone can read them is a list of assertions.

  • 5 public
  • 3 on request
  • 3 held by the client

Public means you can open it right now. On request means it exists and I hold it — ask. Held by the client means it belongs to the organisation it was made for. No entry on this page names a journal, a conference or a DOI, because none of this work has one.

MSc theses

MSc thesis 2024 On request

A study of socioeconomic drivers of river export of multiple pollutants in sub-basins worldwide, and qualitative future storylines for African coastal water pollution

Wageningen University & Research

Modelled multi-pollutant river export across 10,226 sub-basins with MARINA-Multi, identified the socioeconomic drivers statistically, and built qualitative scenario storylines for African coastal waters under climate change.

Methods MARINA-Multi model · Statistical driver analysis · Qualitative scenario storylines

Examined and defended. Not deposited in a public repository — ask and I will send it.

Read the case study →

MSc thesis 2021 On request

Approach to soft path water management: thinking beyond cement, steel and pipes — Freetown as case study

Hunan University

Argued that Freetown's water gap is not primarily a pipe-capacity problem, and developed demand-side, reuse and community-stewardship alternatives scoped for resource-constrained settings.

Methods Systems analysis · Feasibility assessment · Implementation framework design

Defended May 2021, on a full Chinese Government (MOFCOM) scholarship.

Read the case study →

BSc dissertation

BSc dissertation 2017 On request

Mapping groundwater potential in the Freetown Complex: a geophysical approach

University of Sierra Leone

Electrical-resistivity surveying combined with geological and hydrogeological data into GIS potential maps for hard igneous rock, validated by subsequent drilling.

Methods Electrical-resistivity surveying · GIS potential mapping · Field validation

First class honours, graduated top of class. The method went on to inform real siting work.

Dataset 2026 Public

AI carbon factor set — sources, ranges and review dates

sustaintheworld

The machine-readable factor set behind the EcoPrompt Coach and the homepage's AI energy chart: ten models, thirteen grid regions, four cooling profiles, plus PUE, the token-energy model and everyday equivalents — each with a citation, a vintage and a plausible range.

Methods Literature synthesis · Provider disclosure review

Reusable on its own. A test fails the build if any factor loses its source, range or review date.

Code 2026 Public

Journey map generator — reproducible cartography

sustaintheworld

Builds the site's journey map from Natural Earth 50 m coastlines: a region-fitted Natural Earth projection, variable simplification, and deterministic output. Pinned dependencies, and a check that the committed SVG still matches the script.

Methods d3-geo Natural Earth projection · TopoJSON variable simplification

EcoPrompt Coach — web tool and evidence ledger

sustaintheworld

Interactive per-query footprint calculator, with an evidence ledger giving every emission factor a source, publication date, vintage, uncertainty range and review date. Input and output tokens are priced separately, because decode costs several times what prefill does.

Reproducing what is here

Everything public on this page runs from one clone with no build step and no API key. The EcoPrompt Coach and the homepage's energy chart read one factor set, so they cannot quote different numbers. The map regenerates byte-identically from pinned dependencies. The narration is content-addressed, so re-rendering unchanged text costs nothing.

npm install && npm test
runs every suite, the map check and the asset-weight budgets
npm run map:build
regenerates the journey map from Natural Earth data
npm run map:check
proves the committed SVG still matches its generator
npm run budget
measures what a first view actually costs, asset by asset
npm run build:content
regenerates every page derived from content/
npm run voice -- --dry-run
shows what re-rendering the narration would cost, and spends nothing
